---
title: "Multi-State Election Comparisons"
---

```{r}
#| label: setup
#| include: false

library(tidyverse)
library(plotly)
library(DT)
library(scales)

# 1. Load county-level datasets
fl_raw <- read_csv("data/florida/results_county_2024.csv", show_col_types = FALSE)
ca_raw <- read_csv("data/california/results_county_2024.csv", show_col_types = FALSE)
ind_raw <- read_csv("data/indiana/results_county_2024.csv", show_col_types = FALSE)
nc_2026_raw <- read_tsv("data/north_carolina/results_pct_20261103.txt", show_col_types = FALSE, quote = "")

# 2. Standardize North Carolina 2026 Senate county totals
nc_sen <- nc_2026_raw |>
  filter(`Contest Name` == "US SENATE", `Choice Party` %in% c("DEM", "REP")) |>
  group_by(County, `Choice Party`) |>
  summarise(votes = sum(`Total Votes`), .groups = "drop") |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = `Choice Party`, values_from = votes, values_fill = 0) |>
  mutate(
    county_name = str_to_title(County),
    votes_dem = DEM,
    votes_gop = REP,
    total_votes = DEM + REP,
    margin_dem = 100 * (DEM - REP) / total_votes,
    state = "North Carolina (2026 Senate)"
  ) |>
  select(state, county_name, votes_dem, votes_gop, total_votes, margin_dem)

# 3. Standardize Florida, California, and Indiana
fl_clean <- fl_raw |>
  mutate(margin_dem = 100 * (per_dem - per_gop), state = "Florida (2024 Pres)") |>
  select(state, county_name, votes_dem, votes_gop, total_votes, margin_dem)

ca_clean <- ca_raw |>
  mutate(margin_dem = 100 * (per_dem - per_gop), state = "California (2024 Pres)") |>
  select(state, county_name, votes_dem, votes_gop, total_votes, margin_dem)

ind_clean <- ind_raw |>
  mutate(margin_dem = 100 * (per_dem - per_gop), state = "Indiana (2024 Pres)") |>
  select(state, county_name, votes_dem, votes_gop, total_votes, margin_dem)

# Combined dataset across all four states (317 counties)
all_counties <- bind_rows(nc_sen, fl_clean, ca_clean, ind_clean)

# Helper function to generate standardized color-coded DT tables with export buttons
build_county_table <- \(df) {
  datatable(
    df,
    extensions = "Buttons",
    options = list(
      dom = "Bfrtip",
      buttons = list(
        list(extend = "copy", text = "📋 Copy"),
        list(extend = "csv", text = "📥 Download CSV")
      ),
      pageLength = 10,
      autoWidth = TRUE
    ),
    rownames = FALSE
  ) |>
    formatRound(c("Dem Votes", "GOP Votes", "Total Votes"), digits = 0, mark = ",") |>
    formatRound("Dem Margin (%)", digits = 2) |>
    formatStyle(
      "Dem Margin (%)",
      backgroundColor = styleInterval(
        c(-30, -15, -0.01, 0, 15, 30),
        c("#fee2e2", "#fecaca", "#fee2e2", "#f8fafc", "#e0e7ff", "#bfdbfe", "#93c5fd")
      ),
      color = styleInterval(0, c("#991b1b", "#1e40af")),
      fontWeight = "600"
    )
}
```


> [!TIP]
> **Interactive controls:** 
> - Click or double-click items in chart legends to isolate or compare states.
> - Hover over any point to inspect detailed county vote totals.
> - Use the searchable tables to filter counties or export data to CSV.

::: {.panel-tabset}

## All States Comparison

Compare all 317 counties across North Carolina, Florida, California, and Indiana. Notice how urban centers (high turnout) trend Democratic, while smaller rural counties trend Republican.

```{r}
#| label: all-states-scatter
#| echo: false
#| message: false
#| warning: false

all_scatter <- all_counties |>
  mutate(
    hover_text = paste0(
      "<b>", county_name, "</b> (", state, ")<br>",
      "Dem Margin: <b>", sprintf("%+.2f%%", margin_dem), "</b><br>",
      "Turnout: ", comma(total_votes), "<br>",
      "Dem: ", comma(votes_dem), " | GOP: ", comma(votes_gop)
    )
  ) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = total_votes, y = margin_dem, color = state, text = hover_text)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", color = "#64748b", linewidth = 0.8) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.75, size = 2.6) +
  scale_x_log10(labels = comma) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = \(x) paste0(x, "%")) +
  scale_color_manual(values = c(
    "California (2024 Pres)" = "#1d68c4",
    "Florida (2024 Pres)" = "#f97316",
    "Indiana (2024 Pres)" = "#d73027",
    "North Carolina (2026 Senate)" = "#7c3aed"
  )) +
  labs(
    title = "County Margin vs. Turnout (317 Counties)",
    subtitle = "Double-click a state in the legend to isolate it",
    x = "County Turnout (log scale)",
    y = "Democratic Margin (% DEM - % GOP)",
    color = "Dataset"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 13) +
  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 14),
    legend.position = "right"
  )

ggplotly(all_scatter, tooltip = "text")
```

### Statewide Summary

```{r}
#| label: statewide-summary-table
#| echo: false

all_counties |>
  group_by(state) |>
  summarise(
    `Total Counties` = n(),
    `Dem Won Counties` = sum(margin_dem > 0),
    `GOP Won Counties` = sum(margin_dem < 0),
    `Total Turnout` = sum(total_votes),
    `Statewide Margin` = sprintf("%+.2f%%", 100 * (sum(votes_dem) - sum(votes_gop)) / sum(total_votes)),
    `State Winner` = if_else(sum(votes_dem) > sum(votes_gop), "Democrat", "Republican"),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  datatable(
    options = list(dom = "t", paging = FALSE),
    rownames = FALSE
  ) |>
  formatRound(c("Total Counties", "Dem Won Counties", "GOP Won Counties", "Total Turnout"), digits = 0, mark = ",")
```

## Florida vs. North Carolina

Florida shifted substantially toward Republicans over recent election cycles (+13.1%), whereas North Carolina remains a battleground where Democrats won the 2026 Senate seat by 2.1%.

```{r}
#| label: fl-nc-scatter
#| echo: false
#| message: false
#| warning: false

fl_nc_p <- all_counties |>
  filter(state %in% c("North Carolina (2026 Senate)", "Florida (2024 Pres)")) |>
  mutate(
    hover_text = paste0(
      "<b>", county_name, "</b> (", state, ")<br>",
      "Dem Margin: <b>", sprintf("%+.2f%%", margin_dem), "</b><br>",
      "Turnout: ", comma(total_votes), "<br>",
      "DEM: ", comma(votes_dem), " | GOP: ", comma(votes_gop)
    )
  ) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = total_votes, y = margin_dem, color = state, text = hover_text)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", color = "#64748b") +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.75, size = 3) +
  scale_x_log10(labels = comma) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = \(x) paste0(x, "%")) +
  scale_color_manual(values = c(
    "Florida (2024 Pres)" = "#f97316",
    "North Carolina (2026 Senate)" = "#7c3aed"
  )) +
  labs(
    title = "Florida vs. North Carolina County Margins",
    x = "County Turnout (log scale)",
    y = "Democratic Margin (% DEM - % GOP)",
    color = "State"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 13) +
  theme(plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 14))

ggplotly(fl_nc_p, tooltip = "text")
```

### Florida County Results

```{r}
#| label: fl-table
#| echo: false

fl_clean |>
  select(`County` = county_name, `Dem Votes` = votes_dem, `GOP Votes` = votes_gop, `Total Votes` = total_votes, `Dem Margin (%)` = margin_dem) |>
  arrange(desc(`Total Votes`)) |>
  build_county_table()
```

## California vs. North Carolina

California has massive population centers (e.g. Los Angeles County alone with over 3.8 million votes) that lean heavily Democratic, giving it a +30.8% statewide margin compared to North Carolina's closely balanced +2.1%.

```{r}
#| echo: false
#| message: false
#| warning: false
```

## Indiana vs. North Carolina

Indiana demonstrates consistently solid Republican margins across nearly all small and medium counties, with only a few urban exceptions (Marion, Monroe, Lake). In contrast, North Carolina has strong Democratic performance across college towns, the Research Triangle, Charlotte, and the Black Belt.

```{r}

#| echo: false
#| message: false
#| warning: false

ind_nc_p <- all_counties |>
  filter(state %in% c("North Carolina (2026 Senate)", "Indiana (2024 Pres)")) |>
  mutate(
    hover_text = paste0(
      "<b>", county_name, "</b> (", state, ")<br>",

  scale_color_manual(values = c(
```

## County Search Explorer

Search, filter, and compare any of the 317 counties across North Carolina, Florida, California, and Indiana. Type in the search box to find specific counties or click any column header to sort.

```{r}
#| label: all-counties-searchable-table
#| echo: false

all_counties |>
  select(`State` = state, `County` = county_name, `Dem Votes` = votes_dem, `GOP Votes` = votes_gop, `Total Votes` = total_votes, `Dem Margin (%)` = margin_dem) |>
  arrange(desc(`Total Votes`)) |>
  datatable(
    extensions = "Buttons",
    filter = "top",
    options = list(
      dom = "Bfrtip",
      buttons = list(
        list(extend = "copy", text = "📋 Copy"),
        list(extend = "csv", text = "📥 Download CSV")
      ),
      pageLength = 15,
      autoWidth = TRUE
    ),
    rownames = FALSE
  ) |>
  formatRound(c("Dem Votes", "GOP Votes", "Total Votes"), digits = 0, mark = ",") |>
  formatRound("Dem Margin (%)", digits = 2) |>
  formatStyle(
    "Dem Margin (%)",
    backgroundColor = styleInterval(
      c(-30, -15, -0.01, 0, 15, 30),
      c("#fee2e2", "#fecaca", "#fee2e2", "#f8fafc", "#e0e7ff", "#bfdbfe", "#93c5fd")
    ),
    color = styleInterval(0, c("#991b1b", "#1e40af")),
    fontWeight = "600"
  )
```
